$comment: Every user-visible feature and protocol capability of Ghostly. Tests declare what they cover with @feature:<id> (Playwright tag) or // covers: <id> (vitest, Rust). scripts/test-map.mjs checks this file against the tags. Edit by hand: one entry per line, infra, features and paths each sorted by key (npm run test:map -- --fix sorts them; the check fails otherwise), so pull requests adding entries do not conflict. "paths" maps source globs to the features a change there can break (ids, area.* prefixes, "*" for everything, [] for no e2e): npm run test:affected runs the e2e tests tagged with them, and every spec when a changed file matches no glob.

features.title: The installed app's icon counts unread messages (Badging API), leaving muted chats out except a mention that gets through
Sound cues in five categories (payments, identities, connection, chat, interface), one switch each; chat mute, one sound per event, none new in the background
System notifications: explicit permission, private text, no replay after reload
Notification sounds, a persistent preference independent of permission
Unread counts per chat, cleared once the chat is opened
Clear all data leaves nothing behind

The composer's + menu (as WhatsApp's): Payment, Identity, Shared services, Document, Photos & videos and Camera rows with coloured icons; greyed rows say why; arrow keys, Enter, Escape back to +; a sheet on phones
One emoji/GIF panel: category icons, a search field, recent emoji and skin tone per profile, GIFs in columns, and an Emoji | GIF switch remembered per profile

Paste a picture or a file into the composer, or drop files on the chat: a sheet shows the picture (or name and size), a caption, Send and Cancel; several files go as several attachments through + → Document's path; pasted pictures are named "Pasted image <date> <time>.png"; text and rich copies paste as text; groups take none

Before sending, text that looks like a wallet seed (BIP39 with checksum), an nsec, a WIF/xprv key or a 64-hex key next to "private key"/"seed" asks first, and a Cashu token pasted in the text box asks "Send N sats to <contact>?" (amount decoded locally); Cancel is the default; nothing leaves the device to check
Typing in a long chat costs what it does in a short one: a keystroke draws no message rows, the field grows without laying the chat out again, and no :has() rule hangs on the message rows
The emoji/GIF panel stands on the composer inside the chat's column; a sheet on phones
An error in a page shows a recoverable error screen instead of a blank app
Links to other sites open outside the app: a new tab on the web, the system browser on Desktop (any letters in the address)
Home screen: New / Join actions, brand returns home
The interface language can be changed (en, pt, es, fr, it, ja, zh, ar)
Menus (chat ⋮, group ⋮, New) are as wide as their longest row: one line per row in every language, inside the window, a sheet on phones
Phone layout: tab bar, chat as its own screen, compact header
Wallet, Identities, Services, Profile and Settings are routes beside the list; old routes redirect (#/share → #/services)
A page's Back goes home (a sub-page's up to its parent), never through the history; places replace each other; a deep link gets home under it
Ghostly's own Online/Offline switch: offline disables sending, the contact is offered Reconnect
Popovers and dialogs close on Escape / outside click and keep their target
Project links open outside the app without leaving Home
Web: installs as an app (manifest, standalone): Install in Settings when the browser offers it, the Add to Home Screen steps on iPhone and iPad

Web: Install app in the account menu, and a hint above the chat list once the app has been used a little (Not now puts it away for good); Safari gets the steps (Share, Add to Home Screen on iPhone and iPad; File, Add to Dock on a Mac); nothing once installed, nor on Firefox

Web: a service worker keeps the build's own files, so the app opens offline with its saved chats and says Offline; nothing else is ever cached (messages, relays, DHT, API answers, the update check, the sign-in callback)
Web: web+ghostly: links open the invite in the web app and leave the address, like #ghostly1… links
Web: text, links, pictures and files shared from other apps open a Share to… chat picker, then that chat's composer with the text in the draft and the files on the attachment sheet
Web: the app icon's shortcuts: New chat, Scan invite (Join with the camera on), Wallets
Web: a new service worker waits and never swaps the app mid-chat; Reload on New version lets it take over and loads the new build
Reduce motion switch (and prefers-reduced-motion honored)
Right-hand pages (Wallet, Identities, Services, Settings, Profile) hold together at every width
Selects: one look everywhere, a native select's keyboard and screen-reader semantics, a list that clears dialogs and fits phones
The chat list can be dragged wider without squeezing the page below a phone's width
A second tab stays out of the way: one peer per browser
Tech Info shows (and copies) a chat's keys, only a preview of the encryption key
Color theme and light/dark/system mode apply at once and survive a reload
Message bubbles take the colour theme's sent/received colours; text, links, ticks, files, voice, invoices and payments stay readable (WCAG contrast) in every theme, light and dark
Text on the accent colour (buttons, badges, chosen options) takes the theme's on-accent ink, readable in every colour theme, light and dark
Desktop: the Tauri updater checks, downloads and installs
Extension: says a new version is out and points at the download
Web: offers the new version and reloads into it; put aside stays aside; check can be turned off
Settings shows the version being released
The web app says plainly what it cannot do (services, native transports)
IndexedDB snapshot/restore for backups: every store kept, never over an existing database
Backup envelope: encrypted bundle format, versioned, verified on restore
Backup passphrase rules; a wrong passphrase restores nothing
A whole profile backed up to a file and restored as a new profile with its passphrase
A whole profile backed up to S3 and restored as a new profile
Audio call
The caller hangs up while it rings / cancels an unanswered call, devices released
Declining leaves neither side on a call

A call's device menu switches the microphone and camera (replaceTrack, no new offer) and the speaker (setSinkId) live; a device unplugged mid-call falls back to the default with a notice, and one plugged back in offers Switch back

The Linux Desktop's native calls use the microphone, camera and speaker chosen in Settings, found by name among GStreamer's devices (the default, logged, when one is gone), and switch them live from the call's device menu
The Linux Desktop calls with no WebRTC in its WebView: WebRTC in Rust (webrtc-rs), media in GStreamer, with browser and Desktop peers alike; missing GStreamer plugins are named on the call buttons
The lock screen covers a call and keeps it going
A call in a small window leaves the chat usable, follows you out of the chat
A paired chat (every new chat) calls over its live session: start, answer, end (calls/1)
A paired chat's call buttons are off with a reason when it is not live (on DHT, connecting) or the contact cannot take calls
calls/1 and services/1 announced in paired-capabilities after the handshake; paired-call frames carry the signals
A call rings while you are elsewhere in the app; answering takes you to it
The chat holding a call stays loaded while you visit other pages
Screen share from inside a voice or video call (no header button), a notice on both sides, back to the camera or to voice when it stops
Own picture moves, resizes and stays inside the window
Call signaling frames (offer/answer/ICE) over the paired link
An audio call grows a camera and a screen without calling again
Video call: camera on/off, mute, hang up
The screen stays on during a call (Screen Wake Lock), asked again when the page comes back
Layer-0 capability record: derived key, sealed before and after the pin, signed, fits 1,000 bytes, rev only moves forward
A group's or community group's link in a message shows a Join group card: a tap joins through the link, a group already joined opens

A Pubky key (pubky://, pk:) or a DID (did:key|jwk|dht|web) in a message shows an identity card: a badge when a contact proved it (or it is yours), resolved on a tap (did:key and did:jwk on this device, when visible)

A ghostly1 invite (bare or as its ghostly.tools link) in a message shows a card with who sent it; only a tap on Join joins, by the Join dialog's rules: an own invite is refused, one already joined opens its chat; a typo'd checksum stays text
An npub, nprofile, note or nevent (nostr: too) in a message shows a card; the profile or note loads only on a tap, from the person's own relays (named on the card), never from the code's relay hints
A chat from a v0.4 code is a compatibility chat: marked in the header, kept working both ways, and Continue in a new chat sends a new invite inside it

A real v0.4.0 build: its invite opens a compatibility chat in the current app, texts go both ways, Continue in a new chat reaches it as a message it says to open in an updated Ghostly, and it refuses a ghostly1 invite without creating anything
DHT delivery records: encode, seal, publish, resolve, dedupe
DHT publication failures are visible and never claimed as receipt
DHT and live delivery share history; offline text fallback independent of stream fallback
Another participation key on the invite-derived channels is ignored, never a stop, and never replaces the saved contact
Text published while the contact is away survives a sender restart and arrives once
DHT-only chat: text published as records, received once, receipts, drafts across reload

Edit your own sent text in a 1:1 chat (its ⋮, or ↑ in an empty composer): an Editing bar above the composer, an "edited" mark on the bubble, the earlier versions in the message's details; an edit never rings, never counts as unread, never moves the chat

paired-edit / paired-edited on the live session once both sides say edit/1: the whole new text with a number per message (highest wins, at most 100), only the contact's own messages, a receive limit, an edit before its message waits a minute; older apps get nothing

Forward a message (its ⋮ Forward, or Select several then Forward) to up to 5 chats and groups picked by name, most recent first; the copy says ↪ Forwarded (Forwarded many times from 5 hops), never who wrote it; payments, ID cards and call lines have no Forward; groups are offered for texts only; a seed or key asks first

A forwarded picture, video, voice note (its waveform kept), audio file or file goes from the bytes on this device, copied for the new chat: never downloaded again, and a large one still asks the receiver (files/3)

A forwarded text or file carries its hop count `fw`: on paired-message, files/2 pf-start, files/3 pf-offer and a held item's meta, and as the DHT body's fifteenth element (left out when the packet has no room); older apps ignore it
A legacy chat before its data link refuses overlong text, keeps the draft, leaves no bubble
Compatibility chat delivers text through the relay while the other side is away
The sender's app reads a typed link's Open Graph/oEmbed metadata, shows a removable preview in the composer and sends it with the message (Link previews setting)
A received preview renders from the message (title, description, site, thumbnail; YouTube/Vimeo as a video card) without contacting the site
A link preview travels with a paired message as `pv`: bounded, checked against the text, ignored by older apps
geo: URIs and Google/Apple/OpenStreetMap links show a location card; the map loads from OpenStreetMap only on tap
Two apps with no WebRTC in common (Linux Desktop) open On DHT and go live on Iroh or HyperDHT by dialling the native descriptors in each other's capability record, with no text lost or doubled

One chat, one invite: first contact on the DHT and a stream at once; with no transport the chat opens On DHT and goes live by itself; a drop falls back to the DHT and nothing is lost or shown twice; a key mismatch on either path stops both
A deleted message is gone for good, and only here
The connection panel's Details say how contacts are found (DHT direct, or the relay last read) and each relay's health: ok, throttled until, failing until
A multiline draft survives navigation, resizing and Home
Emoji in the composer
GIF search and send

GifCities' rate limit (a 200 HTML page, or a 429) reads as busy, not unavailable: a countdown, Try again off until the wait (30 s doubling to 5 min) is over, remembered for the app session; answers kept per search (20 min) so categories and panels opened again ask nothing, and earlier GIFs or the emoji meanwhile
The GIF panel's category icons are searches of their own: the grid changes with the icon, spins while GifCities answers, and says when nothing loads
A picture address over https shows only once asked; http is never fetched
The chat's join announcement names whoever actually joined
Web addresses become safe links (new tab, no opener/referrer); javascript:/data: never do

A message's details (double-click, long-press or its menu): how it travelled, in plain words and in sections (identity, path, timing, wire, crypto, delivery, file/voice/payment), copyable, with no key ever shown
Nicknames exchanged between paired contacts
Messages written while the contact is away are queued (outbox) and delivered on return
Two people pair from an invite: relay discovery, then peer to peer
A first pairing is live in seconds: fast publish, unblocked reads, tight polls, short attempts; timed step by step
Pairing shows its progress until live: a network scene per stage, plain words, elapsed time, slow notes, failure with Retry, told by the connection icon (the header's only connection element)

A first pairing says how far it got: publishing, waiting, resolving, knocking, answering, connecting, then live or on-dht (with why); failed only for a key mismatch, a rejection, publishing or offline
Delivery and read receipts (ticks)
Reconnect after the contact went away or reloaded; a silent drop comes back by itself
Send and receive text over the paired data link
Paired session handshake, signal exchange and state machine
Connection status control and panel: the status dot, both keys, connected transport, offline, discovery/publication issues
Paired chat persistence (history, pins, contact records) across reloads
Optional verification: one comparison code on both sides, each confirms, remembered
Pin a message from its ⋮ (Pin, Unpin): a bar under the header shows a line of it on both sides, a click scrolls to it and marks it, ✕ unpins; one per chat, a new pin replaces it

paired-pin / paired-pinned on the live session once both sides say pin/1 (message id or empty to unpin, a number, the last pin wins, a receive limit); the pinner says it again on each session until confirmed; older apps drop both

React to a message with an emoji (hover or long-press: a quick bar of six and + for any emoji; or its ⋮ → React): chips under the bubble, mine marked, a click on mine takes it back, on another's adds the same, who reacted on hover; one reaction per person per message; the chat list says who reacted, with no unread count and no message sound

paired-reaction / paired-reacted on the live session once both sides say react/1 (message id, one emoji or empty to take it back, a number per sender, highest wins, a receive limit), on DHT envelopes as trailing elements (13th: the list, 14th: a receipt number) off the live session; older apps drop both

Reply to a message (its ⋮, a hover button, a swipe right on touch): a quote bar above the composer (✕ or Escape cancels), the reply's bubble quotes the original, a tap scrolls to it and marks it; a deleted, unchecked or unknown original is said so

A reply travels with a paired message as `r` (the original's id, a cleaned line of at most 120 code points, its author), in a held text's meta, and over the DHT as its id alone; the receiver checks the id against this chat only; older apps ignore it
A key-like run of 80+ base64/hex characters folds to one line with Show all and Copy

Lines starting with - * • or a number form lists (the author's numbers kept, one nested level, hanging wrap), > lines a quote with a bar, # to ### a bold heading; never inside code; the chat list keeps • and the numbers
Fenced ``` code blocks: monospace, sideways scroll, the language named after the fence highlighted (loaded on first use), Copy; a message that is JSON shows pretty-printed as written

Light formatting shows as written, never as HTML: *bold* (or **bold**), _italic_, ~~strike~~ and `code`, paired within a line and never inside a word, a link or code; the chat list previews it without markers
[text](https://…) shows the text as a link with its host on hover; http(s) only, and text that reads as another address shows the address instead
||Spoilers|| stay covered until tapped or activated by keyboard, are read out as hidden text, and stay hidden in the chat list
A time with its zone (ISO with an offset, "at 14:00 UTC", "3pm GMT+2") shows the reader's local time on hover or tap; times without a zone, scores and versions stay text

Chat timeline scrolling (1:1, groups, communities): at the bottom a new message keeps the view there; scrolled up nothing moves it (anchored on a message, media loading included) and a "↓ N new" pill (a badge on phones) goes to the first new one; my own send goes to the bottom; a plain ↓ when far up; End or Ctrl/Cmd+↓

Search inside a chat (its ⋮ Search, or Ctrl/Cmd+F): only what this device keeps, the text and file names, whatever the case and accents; "3 of 12" newest first, the matches marked, ↑ ↓ (Enter, Shift+Enter) scroll to each and mark it; Escape closes
Typing indicator in 1:1 chats (typing/1 on the live session only): "typing…" in the header and the chat-list row until stop, the message, or 6 s; never stored, never on the DHT
What the chat cannot carry yet waits (a clock beside the time, ⋮ → Cancel sending): a second DHT text, text over 256 bytes, files and Cashu/Lightning requests; a byte counter at 256 while not live
A new chat's creation marker survives the first offline message and a reload
One chat deleted from the chat or the list; the dialog cancels safely
Delete all chats: they stay deleted, settings stay
A contact or member with no name shows as a shortened public key, both ends kept
Pin a chat from the list (no switch), survives reload, unpin from Options
A chat can be named (Escape cancels, blur saves)
A chat's row is two lines: name and time, then the last message with its delivery mark and the unread count; the key is in the tooltip, hover actions move nothing
Chats can be found by name
A contact with no name is shown as "Contact · <start of their key>" with a pattern drawn from their key, never "Anonymous"

Mute one chat's notifications (15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day, until unmuted): its messages arrive and count, with no sound or system notification, a bell mark in the list, a grey unread count; muted and unmuted from the chat's ⋮ or the row's bell (hover or keyboard) without opening the chat; the mute ends by itself, and calls still ring

Older Rust CLI and TypeScript peers interoperate (records, crypto)

Older Rust ghostly-cli recv / watch (NDJSON)
Older Rust ghostly-cli send (flags, env, stdin)
Bitcoin address decoding per network (bech32/bech32m/base58, BIP 173/350)
Capability / version negotiation in the paired handshake
Key derivation, sealing (X25519 / XChaCha20-Poly1305), signatures
Mainline DHT (BEP44) reached directly over UDP from Rust
Frame encoding and limits on the data link
Keet-compatible identity key handling
Liveness: a link that silently stops answering is detected
Peer keys: participation keys, durable pinning, key change rejected
Ghost records: signed Pkarr records published and resolved

A circuit breaker per Pkarr relay: three failures or 429s in a row leave it alone for 1 to 5 minutes (doubling), then one probe; the other relays (or the DHT) take its turns; trips logged without keys
Pkarr relay client: publish/resolve over HTTP, fallbacks, rate limits
Text normalization and size limits
Protocol and app version compatibility checks
Per-chat switch to hold messages for an away contact (consent in the offer)
An expired held item is dropped
A contact whose app does not hold is unaffected
A picture held for an away contact
hold/1: sealed bundles, manifest, presigned GETs, _hold pointer record, bounds
A payment request held for an away contact
The sender's own S3 storage, set up and proven from Profile → Backups, is where held items go
A changed held item is refused
Text held in the sender's S3 while the contact is away, picked up in order
Desktop opens with the peer Rust backs behind it (DHT direct in Settings → Network)
src/desktop/ invocations survive in the bundle (check:desktop-bundle)
Rust keypair / encryption commands match the TypeScript protocol
The desktop app keeps a log of discovery and pairing steps (ghostly.log under its log directory, and stderr)
Rust local_fetch serves shared services
Native private notifications
Desktop opens lightning:/bitcoin: links via Tauri
did:dht documents: DNS records in the Pkarr packet of an Ed25519 key (the spec's vectors), strictly parsed, resolved through Pkarr relays
did:dht interop: an independent implementation (@web5/dids) resolves the DID Ghostly publishes, and Ghostly resolves one it publishes

Every profile has a did:dht of a key of its own (never a chat's): published while online, the same packet put again every hour, re-signed only when the document changes; the identity key alone unless the person lists identities

Public DID, in the Ghostly card's details: the did:dht with copy and QR, a switch per identity (off by default) that lists it in the document's alsoKnownAs, and a warning that the document is public to everyone and cached
The engine runs in the extension's offscreen document; UI attaches over a port
The extension and the web app chat, share files and call each other

An audio file (MP3, M4A/AAC, Ogg/Opus, WAV, FLAC; not a voice message) plays in its bubble: name, play, a seek bar, time and the speed voice messages share; one at a time; a large one shows Download <size> first; a type this device cannot play offers Download

Download from a message's menu: a voice message or file is saved (the system save dialog on Desktop, a browser download elsewhere), a voice message as "Ghostly voice <date> <time>" in its own format, or converted here to MP3 (Download as MP3); greyed while it is still arriving, when it failed or when it is gone

A picture's bubble has its box before the picture loads: from the size its sender said, else from its first bytes here (a placeholder until then); one that loads another shape is shown as it is; a picture link keeps a 120 px placeholder until it loads

A picture's announcement may carry its size as shown, read from its first bytes (PNG, JPEG with EXIF orientation, GIF, WebP) by the apps and the CLI (files/2, files/3, held items); old apps ignore it, a bad one is dropped
The sender's SHA-256 is checked on what the receiver stored; a file that does not match is deleted and both sides say so
Per contact, at most 16 offers wait and 3 files arrive at once; an unanswered offer ends after a week; apps without files/3 keep files/2 and 100 MB
Files of any size (files/3): above 25 MB, or past 500 MB from one contact, the receiver accepts or declines, seeing its free space; a file larger than the contact's room is refused before it is sent
A file that stopped arriving offers Ask again, and asks by itself after 30 s with nothing: the sender goes on from the bytes held here

A file or voice note that stopped moving (a minute with nothing, or unfinished since the app started) offers Send again: offered again under its id, it goes on from what the receiver holds, one message on each side
A file transfer goes on from the last stored byte after a drop, a transport switch or a restart; either side pauses, resumes or cancels; progress shows speed and time left
Files over the legacy data channel
Images shown inline
Files peer to peer (files/2), arrive intact (checksum)
Received files persist across reloads
File sizes are shown in B / KB / MB
A file over the platform's limit is refused before anything is sent

A video's announcement may carry its length, size and a small JPEG of its first frame (files/2, files/3, held items); old apps ignore it, a bad one only drops the poster

A video plays in its bubble: poster with its length and a big play button, native controls (seek, time, mute, full screen), one at a time, paused when scrolled away; a large one shows Download <size> first; a type this device cannot play offers Download

On Desktop a video too large to hold in the page (over 64 MiB) plays and seeks from the stored file, served in ranges by the ghostly-file scheme: a random token per play, only to the Ghostly window, never a path
One voice message plays at a time; the next one from the same sender follows on its own
A voice message or an audio file playing shows on the lock screen and in the system's media controls, which play, pause, seek (and skip to the next voice message) (Media Session)
A voice message is a file whose announcement carries its length and waveform (files/2 and held items); a bad description only drops the player
A voice message plays in its bubble: waveform progress, scrubbing, time, 1x/1.5x/2x, unplayed mark for received ones
Hold the mic to record a voice message and release to send; slide to cancel or lock; hands-free with pause, preview, delete; click, Esc and Enter on desktop

A member who was away catches up from any member who holds what it missed
A member who was away is caught up by whoever is there, not only by the author

Someone who joins later reads nothing sent before

A request to a whole community, paid once: first valid payment wins, later ones refused unredeemed

Everyone reads everyone through hubs the online members elect
The group header's connection control: each member's edge reachable or not, its transport, last seen
Create a private group

Invite contacts; accept or decline an invitation
Leave a group (and it leaves the list)
Enable / disable a shareable group link

A replaced link reaches nobody
